signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Policy Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows USD outperforming as the strongest G10 currency with a 1W average of +0.590% across 9 pairs, while SEK anchors the bottom as the weakest laggard with a 1W average of -0.637% across 2 pairs, establishing a wide 1.227% leader-to-laggard spread. USD/SEK trades at 9.7730, holding above its SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200 cluster at 9.5760, 9.5920, and 9.3510 respectively. The underlying macro divergence is driven by central bank policy, where the Fed holds rates at 3.75% against the Riksbank at 1.75%, generating a 200bp carry advantage for USD. This macro gap is further reinforced by economic surprises, as the SEK Economic Surprise Index prints a strong negative -29.2 while the US Index remains steady at +0.5. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK; broad rate differential and data divergence favor ongoing upside momentum. Catalyst: FOMC interest rate decision today at 18:00 UTC — Fed hold at 3.75% expected. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% or Fed signals aggressive future easing, unwinding the bilateral theme setup.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Position Rebuilding
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.06, holding below its SMA20 at 157.14, SMA50 at 159.40, and SMA200 at 158.39. Options markets exhibit heavy downside hedging demand, with the 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal showing a strong put skew of -1.98. Conversely, CFTC Leveraged Funds net short positioning in JPY covered substantially with a WoW delta of +58,042 to sit at net -53,255 (30th percentile of its 52-week range). While the Fed at 3.75% versus BoJ at 1.0% generates a +264bp OIS carry advantage for USD (SOFR 3.62% vs TONA 0.98%), the options skew and speculative short covering highlight active downside protection ahead of policy events. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; persistent put options demand and JPY short covering limit upside momentum. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision and press conference on 18 Sep. Risk: Sustained break above SMA20 at 157.14 or dovish BoJ guidance restoring carry-seeking flows.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Data Repricing + Positioning Crowding
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3477, holding below its SMA20 at 1.3557 and SMA50 at 1.3484, while remaining above its SMA200 at 1.3455. UK August headline CPI accelerated to 3.1% YoY matching expectations, maintaining pressure on the Bank of England ahead of its policy meeting. CFTC speculative positioning shows Leveraged Funds net long GBP at +40,361 contracts, which represents the 86th percentile of its 52-week range (z-score +1.02), signaling elevated positioning density. Option implied volatility sits at 5.4% against a 30-day realized volatility of 3.6%, reflecting a +1.9% volatility risk premium as markets hedge upcoming central bank decisions. Trade bias: Neutral/cautious GBP/USD; crowded spec longs and moving average overhead resistance limit immediate upside despite firm inflation. Catalyst: BoE interest rate decision on 17 Sep. Risk: Unwind of crowded speculative longs if BoE votes reveal a dovish shift.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Crowding + Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7132, holding below its SMA20 at 0.7172 while remaining above its SMA50 at 0.7077 and SMA200 at 0.7008. CFTC Leveraged Funds positioning is heavily crowded long at net +48,379 contracts, sitting at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range (z-score +1.72). In the options market, 1M ATM implied volatility of 7.5% trades well above 30-day realized volatility of 5.3%, creating an elevated Volatility Risk Premium of +2.1% that underscores heightened downside hedging demand. A carry advantage exists for AUD via RBA at 4.35% versus Fed at 3.75% (-73bp OIS basis favoring AUD), but stalled positioning additions indicate late-trend caution. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; upper-decile spec long crowding limits extension upside. Catalyst: FOMC interest rate decision today at 18:00 UTC. Risk: Sharp unwind in speculative longs if global risk sentiment deteriorates.

signals.title: EUR/CHF — Institutional Positioning vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/CHF trades at 0.9451, maintaining an upside bias as the ECB policy rate of 2.65% provides a +265bp carry premium over the SNB rate of 0.00%. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme short reading of 90% short against 10% long, directly diverging from CFTC institutional flows where Leveraged Funds hold net short CHF positions at -13,968 contracts (12th percentile of its 52-week range). Swiss economic data remains strong with a CHF Economic Surprise Index of +23.9, but structural carry differential and retail fade positioning support the pair's floor. Trade bias: Long EUR/CHF; retail extreme short positioning and positive ECB-SNB carry differential favor upside continuation. Catalyst: SNB interest rate decision on 24 Sep. Risk: Sudden risk-off shock triggering CHF safe-haven flows and compressing cross-carry.
